transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Wednesday, November 25. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. 'Are we beggars?' Congress fumes as Akhilesh offers 26 seats for UP polls. Tensions have surfaced between the Samajwadi Party and Congress ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, with Congress MP Imran Masood asking, "Are we beggars?" over SP's offer of 26 seats. While Congress is seeking 120 seats, Akhilesh Yadav has stressed winnability and called for further discussions to defeat the BJP. Meerut woman escapes hotel room after assault, ex-boyfriend catches her, drags her back. A 24-year-old woman escaped a hotel in Meerut where her ex-boyfriend confined and assaulted her. She reported that he chased her after she fled the hotel room on Tuesday. The incident was captured on CCTV and prompted police intervention following alerts from passersby. The suspect, identified as Mohd Salman, fled across rooftops when police arrived at the scene quickly. 'They are always meditating': Sindarov notices a pattern among Indian chess players. The remark came during the post-match press conference after defending champion Gukesh, playing with black, drew the first game against the Uzbek challenger. 'Will take Bangladesh by Dec 16': Bengal minister vows revenge for killings of Hindus. West Bengal minister Arjun Singh has claimed that India would take over Bangladesh by December 16 and vowed revenge for the killings of Hindus in the neighbouring country. His remarks come amid tensions over former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's proposed return from India, with Dhaka warning that she would face arrest and be brought back in handcuffs. IBM tells visa holders in its biggest division: Leave the US or leave IBM by Dec 31. IBM is ending US visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in IBM Consulting, its biggest division with over 150,000 employees. Affected H-1B workers can relocate to IBM roles outside the US, mostly in India, or leave the company by December 31, 2026. The move comes amid the US administration's crackdown on H-1B visas and foreign tech hiring, including a one-time $100,000 filing fee. 'Not a single bogus vote to be added': Akhilesh asks SP workers to monitor ECI. Akhilesh Yadav has called on Samajwadi Party workers to monitor electoral roll activities ahead of the upcoming elections. He emphasized that no bogus votes should be added and no genuine votes should be removed from the lists. Yadav expressed concerns regarding the credibility of Electronic Voting Machines, reflecting public scepticism and recent controversies. He also urged Congress to identify additional winnable constituencies for the seat-sharing negotiations. Study of 18,457 skeletons finds men in Southeast Asia lost 7 inches in height. Innovative farming technologies have surprisingly led to a decrease in human height over millennia, as revealed by research analyzing thousands of skeletal remains. In Southeast Asia, notable reductions were observed wherein the average male height decreased from 5 feet 10 inches to just 5 feet 3 inches. This shift might be attributed to heightened population density, which adversely affected nutrition and health, thereby altering growth trends across different regions. 'Lot of runs here': Forget pacer-friendly reputation, Hagley pitch can flatten out. "I think every game's different, every surface you play on is slightly different as well. And I think there's been a lot of runs scored here of late as well," Henry said at a press conference on Wednesday. What is the Fifth Amendment, and why is Trump urging Jensen Huang not to invoke it. US president Donald Trump has urged Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to tell the truth when he faces congressional questioning next week. Groww told to refund rupees 11.85L to Bengaluru woman after tech glitch. Ranjana Priya's investment of rupees 8.12 lakhs in the Groww app initially flourished, reaching rupees 12.7 lakhs. However, upon seeking a redemption of rupees 10 lakhs, she was shocked to see her portfolio plummet to just rupees 84,508. After numerous complaints went unanswered, the Bengaluru Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission deemed Groww liable for unfair practices, ultimately ordering them to refund rupees 11.85 lakhs plus interest and compensation.

Microscopic pollen grains trapped in the ancient coatings are now helping scientists reconstruct where the vessel may have traveled and undergone repairs more than two millennia ago. Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat. Researchers have discovered a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression. Known as "circadian depression," it is linked to the body's internal clock and is associated with night owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe symptoms. Traditional antidepressants often work less effectively for these individuals, potentially explaining why some people struggle to find relief. transcript.title: Across India
transcript.text: Turning to the big national stories. 'Not a single bogus vote to be added': Akhilesh tells SP workers to monitor election commission activities. Akhilesh Yadav has called on Samajwadi Party workers to monitor electoral roll activities ahead of the upcoming elections. He emphasized that no bogus votes should be added and no genuine votes should be removed from the lists. Yadav expressed concerns regarding the credibility of Electronic Voting Machines, reflecting public scepticism and recent controversies. He also urged Congress to identify additional winnable constituencies for the seat-sharing negotiations. 'Will take Bangladesh by December 16': Bengal minister Arjun Singh vows revenge for killings of Hindus. West Bengal minister Arjun Singh has claimed that India would take over Bangladesh by December 16 and vowed revenge for the killings of Hindus in the neighbouring country. His remarks come amid tensions over former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's proposed return from India, with Dhaka warning that she would face arrest and be brought back in handcuffs. Passport has discrepancies in place of birth: CJP's Saurav Das rendered ineligible for foreign travel. CJP activist Saurav Das has been served a notice by the Regional Passport Office regarding his birth documents. The notice requires him to respond within seven days to clarify discrepancies in his documents. If he fails to provide a satisfactory explanation, his passport may be impounded under the Passports Act. A pending re-verification will determine his eligibility for international travel once cleared. 'Crores of devotees let down': BJP slams Vijay govt for defying SC order on Deepam row. The controversy over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram hills escalated on Wednesday, with BJP national general secretary BL Santhosh accusing the TVK-led government of defying the Supreme Court's interim order and warning that Chief Minister Vijay's government would face a "civilisational and legal challenge". Amit Shah: Kartarpur corridor to open after review. Union home minister Amit Shah expressed that the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor will only reopen after addressing prevailing security issues. This corridor, which offers hassle-free access for pilgrims, was shut down following security alerts linked to Operation Sindoor. Shah highlighted the need to keep national security discussions free from political influences, while also pointing out that the corridor's placement in Pakistan stemmed from Congress party oversights during partition. ICMR: Over 50 per cent of women of reproductive age anaemic. 'Two-thirds of adolescents deficient in Vitamin B12' NSA Ajit Doval, Maldives defence minister discuss security ties at Colombo meet. National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Maldives defense minister Hassan Rasheed discussed security cooperation at the Colombo Security Conclave. This meeting marked the first high-level interaction between the two countries since President Mohamed Muizzu's recent visit to Pakistan. During that visit, Maldives signed 20 agreements with Pakistan related to defense and maritime issues. Additionally, Muizzu called for resuming the Saarc summit process to enhance regional cooperation. PM Modi, Merz say India-EU FTA will unlock new opportunities. Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently engaged in discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, focused on enhancing the India-Germany Strategic Partnership. The conversation covered various critical areas including trade, investment, defence, and cutting-edge technologies, underscoring both nations' dedication to global peace. As they commemorate 75 years of diplomatic ties, they aim to bolster cooperation across essential sectors while sharing insights on regional issues of common interest. From ghat to gallery, Banaras set for brush with art. The CII Banaras Biennale is set to commence on November 27, culminating on December 31. This unique event aims to intertwine the ancient and modern art scenes, presenting the vibrant culture of Banaras. Activities will unfold at numerous venues, including the distinguished Bharatiya Kala Bhavan. By fostering partnerships between cultural institutions and industry, the Biennale aspires to spark rich dialogues, bridging diverse artistic expressions with their historical narratives. Government plans multi-year motor insurance for cars, bikes; no insurance, no fuel pilot at 10 petrol pumps in NCR. The road transport ministry is gearing up to introduce initiatives to lower the incidence of uninsured vehicles on Indian roads. Key proposals include establishing a unified insurance premium for different vehicle types. Furthermore, traffic violations recorded against vehicle owners could potentially affect their insurance costs. A trial of the 'no insurance, no fuel' strategy will be initiated at select fuel stations. Dalai Lama, office allotted bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi. The Centre has assigned a government bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama. This official accommodation aims to facilitate his visits to the national capital and provide comfort. Members of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile have welcomed this arrangement as a supportive gesture towards their community. Gaden Phodrang, the Dalai Lama's office, was registered as a private trust in India in 2011. BSF constable dies by suicide in Arnia. In a tragic incident, Deva Nand Majhi, a young BSF constable stationed in Jammu and Kashmir, reportedly took his own life at a security camp. The shocking event unfolded in the Arnia border region late Monday night when he allegedly utilized his service weapon. Originally from Katsa in Bihar's Saran district, his remains have been sent to GMC Jammu's mortuary for autopsy. Cops stop Mehbooba's Sheshnag trek amid BRO construction row. Concerns are mounting among political leaders, notably PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, regarding the construction activities near Sheshnag Lake. Environmental advocates and Congress members underscore the area's ecological sensitivity. The Border Roads Organisation defends its initiatives as critical for ensuring safety for pilgrims on the Amarnath Yatra route. Detractors warn that development could endanger local ecosystems, revealing a broader conflict between aspirations for growth and the need for environmental conservation. Rijiju heaps praise on Jammu and Kashmir Waqf Board. Union minister Kiren Rijiju praised the Jammu and Kashmir Waqf Board for its remarkable contributions across various sectors, particularly citing the development projects at the Hazratbal and Baba Reshi shrines. Rijiju remarked that this waqf board serves as a role model for similar entities nationwide. He also pledged to aid in skill development and training programs aimed at empowering the youth of Kashmir. 'Hold serious discussions with us': Akhilesh's public message to Congress on UP seat-sharing. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday called for a consensus-based seat-sharing deal with Congress for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, saying both parties must prioritise winnability over the number of seats.

transcript.text: And finally, here is what is happening around the world. Indian government has 'lost the plot', says 'cockroach' leader barred from UK flight. Published extracts from the late pontiff's diary claim one of the visions happened "in the choir loft" during Mass. Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book. The publisher of an essay on coercive control apologises for "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication". Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine. Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine. Car bomb tears through Colombian city wounding more than 20.
